Reading order: main text right page top to bottom; the left strip is a margin of the facing page and is transcribed as notes.

main_text.p: 18 Forma tria habet officia, 1. Determinate rem constituere, unde forma vocatur. 2. Effentialiter eam distinguere, unde appellatur differentia. 3. Efficere operationes & actiones quarum est principium, unde actus nominatur.
19 Finis exurgit ex conjunctione materiæ & formæ,& est illa bonitas vel perfectio rei qua elt ad operationem & usum apta.

20 Bonitas hæc in efficientis intentione,est adjuvans causa; ufus ad quem tendit, est effectum; res vel persona cui inservit in usu,est objectum:ad hæc tamen omnia propter affinitatem, finis nomen solet applicari:bonitas vel aptitudo ad usum est proprie finalis causa;appetitio ejus impellens efficientem,est finis intentionis; usus est secundarius finis cujus; res vel persona ad quam petat est finis cui.& in his omnibus generibus,unus aliquando finis operis dicitur;& alius operantis: sed scopus operantis à natura operis alienus, per accidens, tantum finis dicitur operationis.

21 Quamvis causæ distinctæ sint essentia & definitione, res tamen quæ vi causarum fit unicam habet naturam, quæ licet arguatur à singulis causis, tamen ab efficiente ut à principio quod primam vim exerit

page.notes: Left strip is the cropped facing page (partly illegible, Latin and Italian fragments of text such as "unde", "tanquam", "dicitur"); not transcribed in full because it is cut off by the gutter and too fragmentary to read reliably. The main text's last line is continued on the next page as "exerit" printed at the right.
